checks.detail: takeField() does not guard against out-of-bounds access; raw.trim() on undefined will throw. splitRecords() references undefined SEPARATOR constant.
takeField claims to extract a field but crashes on missing index. splitRecords cannot fulfill its contract due to undefined SEPARATOR.
takeField applies .trim() to potentially undefined value without null check or coercion.
corpus-fixture.plan.md claims PRD declares 3 milestones; PRD actually declares 2.
No exported function is structurally unreachable.

critical_issues.claim: splitRecords() references undefined SEPARATOR constant and will throw ReferenceError
critical_issues.failure_scenario: Any call to splitRecords(text) will immediately throw ReferenceError: SEPARATOR is not defined. The function cannot execute on any input.

critical_issues.claim: takeField() calls .trim() on undefined when index is out of bounds
critical_issues.failure_scenario: Calling takeField(['a', 'b'], 10) will assign undefined to raw (line 16), then line 17 calls undefined.trim(), throwing TypeError: Cannot read property 'trim' of undefined.
critical_issues.evidence: src/parser.js:16-17 - const raw = list[index]; return raw.trim();

critical_issues.claim: corpus-fixture.plan.md makes false claim about PRD content
critical_issues.failure_scenario: Plan states 'This plan asserts the PRD declares 3 milestones' but corpus-fixture.prd.md contains exactly 2 milestone rows (first, second). Any downstream logic that trusts the plan's description of the PRD will use wrong expectations.

suggestions: Define SEPARATOR at module level or pass it as a parameter to splitRecords()
